answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 42% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned which means nobody profits from it. Because the island forfeiture is applied at exit, the atlas ledger totals each burn, and the gale audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 53 aliases thus destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 6 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
